1: # 🎵 Music Generation — AI Background Music via Google Lyria 3
2: 
3: > **Skill for:** Stage 4 (Voice) / Stage 6 (Assembly) — background music production
4: > **Creates:** Copyright-safe, mood-matched BGM for every Stickman video
5: > **Tool:** Google Lyria 3 (primary) | YouTube Audio Library / Pixabay (fallback)
6: > **Rule:** Every video MUST have background music. No exceptions. BGM is not optional.
7: 
8: ---
9: 
10: ## When To Use
11: 
12: Use this skill for **every single video**. Background music is one of the 5 mandatory audio layers (see `audio_production.md` § 2).
13: 
14: Say: **"Use the music generation skill. My script sections are: [list moods]."**
15: 
16: ### Trigger Points in the Pipeline
17: 
18: | Stage | Action |
19: |---|---|
20: | **Stage 3 (Script)** | Tag each script section with a mood from the palette below |
21: | **Stage 4 (Voice)** | Generate music segments in parallel with voiceover sections |
22: | **Stage 6 (Assembly)** | Layer music under voice at -18 dB, apply crossfades and swells |
23: 
24: ---
25: 
26: ## 1 · The 6 Music Moods
27: 
28: Every script section maps to exactly ONE of these 6 moods. No exceptions, no custom moods.
29: 
30: | # | Mood | When to Use | Instruments | Tempo | Feel |
31: |---|---|---|---|---|---|
32: | 1 | **Neutral / Context** | Default narration, scene-setting, introducing a topic | Soft synth pads, lo-fi ambient, filtered piano | 60-80 BPM | Background wallpaper — present but invisible |
33: | 2 | **Tense / Dangerous** | Survival stakes, danger, "you die" moments, villains | Dark ambient drones, sub-bass, distorted pads, sparse percussion | 70-100 BPM | Dread without panic |
34: | 3 | **Philosophical / Reflective** | Moral lessons, "what does this mean?", closing thoughts | Solo cello, nylon guitar, Rhodes piano, acoustic strings | 50-70 BPM | Quiet contemplation, slight melancholy |
35: | 4 | **Escalation / Countdown** | List entries building, "and it gets worse", rising stakes | Ticking percussion, rising synths, layered loops | 90-120 BPM (accelerating) | Pressure building, can't look away |
36: | 5 | **Climax / Peak Reveal** | The #1 reveal, biggest twist, "here's what actually happened" | Orchestra hit + sub-bass + full pad swell | Peaks then drops | Impact → silence → voice returns |
37: | 6 | **Resolution / CTA** | Final thoughts, subscribe moment, "thanks for watching" | Acoustic guitar, warm pad, gentle keys | 60-80 BPM | Warm, resolved, safe landing |
38: 
39: ---
40: 
41: ## 2 · Lyria 3 Prompt Templates (Copy-Paste Ready)
42: 
43: > **How to use:** Open [Google AI Music (Lyria 3)](https://aitestkitchen.withgoogle.com/tools/music-fx), paste the prompt, generate, download.
44: > **Format:** Always request WAV or highest quality available. Convert to 48 kHz / 24-bit stereo if needed.
45: 
46: ### Mood 1 — Neutral / Context
47: 
48: ```
49: Soft ambient electronic, 70 BPM, neutral key. Gentle reverb synth pads with 
50: filtered warm piano appearing every 4 bars. Lo-fi texture, slight vinyl crackle 
51: underneath. Feeling: calm documentary narration, background wallpaper that doesn't 
52: distract. No drums, no percussion, no vocals. Subtle and unobtrusive. 
53: [DURATION] seconds.
54: ```
55: 
56: ### Mood 2 — Tense / Dangerous
57: 
58: ```
59: Dark ambient electronic, 85 BPM, minor key. Low sub-bass drone underneath, 
60: distorted synth pads with slow LFO modulation. Sparse metallic percussion hits 
61: every 8 bars. Feeling: something terrible is about to happen, primal dread, 
62: 2 AM unease. No drums, no vocals. Ominous but controlled, never chaotic. 
63: [DURATION] seconds.
64: ```
65: 
66: ### Mood 3 — Philosophical / Reflective
67: 
68: ```
69: Melancholic ambient, 60 BPM. Solo reverb piano with long sustain, single cello 
70: note held underneath. Nylon guitar plucks appearing occasionally. Feeling: 
71: sitting alone at night thinking about the meaning of life. Bittersweet, 
72: contemplative, slightly sad but not depressing. No drums, no percussion, 
73: no vocals. Spacious and breathing. [DURATION] seconds.
74: ```
75: 
76: ### Mood 4 — Escalation / Countdown
77: 
78: ```
79: Building electronic ambient, starting at 90 BPM accelerating to 110 BPM. 
80: Layered synth arpeggios that add a new element every 15 seconds. Subtle 
81: ticking percussion pulse underneath. Rising filter sweep on main pad. 
82: Feeling: countdown, pressure mounting, can't look away, each moment more 
83: intense. No heavy drums, no vocals. Builds but never fully releases. 
84: [DURATION] seconds.
85: ```
86: 
87: ### Mood 5 — Climax / Peak Reveal
88: 
89: ```
90: Cinematic ambient swell, 80 BPM. All elements build to a single peak: 
91: deep sub-bass, swelling orchestra-style synth pads, distant choir-like 
92: texture. Crescendo over 20 seconds to maximum intensity, then DROP to 
93: near-silence. Feeling: the moment everything clicks — awe, goosebumps, 
94: revelation. No vocals. End on a single sustained low note fading out. 
95: [DURATION] seconds.
96: ```
97: 
98: ### Mood 6 — Resolution / CTA
99: 
100: ```
101: Warm acoustic ambient, 65 BPM. Gentle fingerpicked acoustic guitar pattern, 
102: soft warm synth pad underneath, subtle Rhodes electric piano chords every 
103: 4 bars. Feeling: the story is over, everything is resolved, safe and warm. 
104: Gentle fade-out over final 5 seconds. No drums, no percussion, no vocals. 
105: Comforting and final. [DURATION] seconds.
106: ```
107: 
108: ---
109: 
110: ## 3 · Volume Rules
111: 
112: > **The #1 Rule: If the viewer can hum the melody while watching, the music is TOO LOUD.**
113: 
114: | Parameter | Value | Why |
115: |---|---|---|
116: | **Perceived volume** | 12% | Music is subliminal — felt, not heard |
117: | **dB level** | -18 dB relative to voiceover | Measured against voice at 0 dB reference |
118: | **Swell at climax** | Temporarily +3 to +5 dB (up to -13 dB) | Brief emotional spike, then return |
119: | **Under reveals** | Drop to -∞ dB (silence) | Part of strategic silence protocol |
120: | **Fade-in at start** | 3-5 seconds | Never start at full volume |
121: | **Fade-out at end** | 5 seconds | Gentle exit under CTA |
122: 
123: ### FFMPEG Volume Commands
124: 
125: ```bash
126: # Set music to -18 dB
127: ffmpeg -i music_raw.wav -af "volume=-18dB" -c:a pcm_s24le music_leveled.wav
128: 
129: # Fade in (3s) + Fade out (5s ending at 535s) + level
130: ffmpeg -i music_raw.wav -af "afade=t=in:st=0:d=3,afade=t=out:st=535:d=5,volume=-18dB" music_ready.wav
131: 
132: # Swell at climax (boost 5 dB from 360s to 375s)
133: ffmpeg -i music_track.wav -af "volume=-18dB,volume=enable='between(t,360,375)':volume=5dB" music_swell.wav
134: ```
135: 
136: > [!CAUTION]
137: > Music must **never** compete with voice for spectral space. Avoid tracks with:
138: > - Vocals or vocal samples
139: > - Prominent mid-range melodies (300-3000 Hz = voice range)
140: > - Sharp transients or loud percussion hits
141: 
142: ---
143: 
144: ## 4 · Duration Guidance
145: 
146: ### How Long Should Each Music Segment Be?
147: 
148: Map your script sections to moods, then use these duration guidelines:
149: 
150: | Script Section | Typical Mood | Duration | % of Video |
151: |---|---|---|---|
152: | Hook (opening 30s) | Neutral or Tense | 30-60 seconds | 5-10% |
153: | Context / Setup | Neutral | 60-120 seconds | 15-25% |
154: | Escalation / List | Escalation | 60-150 seconds | 15-25% |
155: | Main Reveal | Climax | 20-40 seconds | 4-8% |
156: | Consequences / Analysis | Tense or Philosophical | 60-90 seconds | 12-18% |
157: | Closing / Philosophy | Philosophical or Resolution | 60-90 seconds | 12-18% |
158: | CTA | Resolution | 15-30 seconds | 3-5% |
159: 
160: ### Duration Rules
161: 
162: 1. **Total music ≈ 85% of video length** — music plays under voice for most of the video.
163: 2. **Remaining 15%** = strategic silences + transitions + brief unscored moments.
164: 3. **Minimum segment length: 20 seconds** — anything shorter sounds like a glitch.
165: 4. **Maximum segment length: 150 seconds** — anything longer gets monotonous.
166: 5. **Generate segments slightly LONGER than needed** — trim in assembly. Lyria 3 may add intros/outros you'll cut.
167: 
168: ### Typical 8-10 Minute Video Music Map
169: 
170: ```
171: TIME    0:00    1:00    2:00    3:00    4:00    5:00    6:00    7:00    8:00    9:00
172: MOOD    |-Neutral-|--Tense--|---Escalation---|--CLIMAX--|--Philosophical--|--Resol--|
173: VOLUME  |fade▲   -18dB      -18dB           ▲swell▼silence    -18dB        fade▼   |
174: ```
175: 
176: ---
177: 
178: ## 5 · Transition Rules
179: 
180: ### Crossfade Between Mood Changes
181: 
182: When the script mood shifts, **crossfade** the outgoing track into the incoming track. Never hard-cut between music segments.
183: 
184: | Transition Type | Duration | When |
185: |---|---|---|
186: | **Standard crossfade** | 2-3 seconds | Any mood change that isn't a reveal |
187: | **Quick crossfade** | 1-1.5 seconds | Fast-paced escalation sequences |
188: | **Silence gap** | 1-1.5 seconds of zero audio | Before major reveals (strategic silence) |
189: | **Swell → Drop** | Music swells +3-5 dB → cuts to silence → voice returns | Climax / #1 reveal moment |
190: 
191: ### FFMPEG Crossfade Command
192: 
193: ```bash
194: # Crossfade two music segments (3-second overlap)
195: ffmpeg \
196:   -i music_segment_01.wav \
197:   -i music_segment_02.wav \
198:   -filter_complex "\
199:     [0:a]afade=t=out:st=58:d=3[a1]; \
200:     [1:a]afade=t=in:st=0:d=3[a2]; \
201:     [a1][a2]acrossfade=d=3:c1=tri:c2=tri[out]" \
202:   -map "[out]" -c:a pcm_s24le music_crossfaded.wav
203: ```
204: 
205: ### Transition Map for a Standard Video
206: 
207: ```
208: Section 1 (Neutral) ──crossfade 3s──▶ Section 2 (Tense)
209: Section 2 (Tense)   ──crossfade 2s──▶ Section 3 (Escalation)
210: Section 3 (Escalation) ──swell+drop──▶ [SILENCE 1.5s] ──▶ Section 4 (Climax)
211: Section 4 (Climax)  ──crossfade 3s──▶ Section 5 (Philosophical)
212: Section 5 (Philo.)  ──crossfade 2s──▶ Section 6 (Resolution)
213: Section 6 (Resolution) ──fade out 5s──▶ [END]
214: ```
215: 
216: ---
217: 
218: ## 6 · File Organization
219: 
220: ```
221: audio/music/
222: ├── generated/                        ← Lyria 3 outputs (raw)
223: │   ├── [video_slug]_neutral_01.wav
224: │   ├── [video_slug]_tense_01.wav
225: │   ├── [video_slug]_escalation_01.wav
226: │   ├── [video_slug]_climax_01.wav
227: │   ├── [video_slug]_philosophical_01.wav
228: │   └── [video_slug]_resolution_01.wav
229: ├── leveled/                          ← After volume adjustment (-18 dB)
230: │   └── [video_slug]_[mood]_leveled.wav
231: └── assembled/                        ← Final crossfaded music track
232:     └── [video_slug]_music_full.wav
233: ```
234: 
235: **File naming convention:** `[video_slug]_[mood]_[take_number].wav`
236: - Example: `ancient_night_tense_02.wav` = Ancient Night video, tense mood, second take
237: 
238: ---
239: 
240: ## 7 · Copyright-Safe Fallback Sources
241: 
242: If Lyria 3 produces an unusable track (too busy, wrong mood, artifacts), use these pre-cleared sources:
243: 
244: | Source | Cost | License | Best For | Search Tips |
245: |---|---|---|---|---|
246: | **YouTube Audio Library** | Free | Pre-cleared for YouTube | All moods | Filter by mood + "ambient" or "cinematic" |
247: | **Pixabay Music** | Free | CC0, no attribution | Neutral, Resolution | Search: "ambient background", "lo-fi documentary" |
248: | **Unminus** | Free | All free, curated | Philosophical, Neutral | Small library but high quality |
249: | **Epidemic Sound** | $15/mo | Full YouTube license, stems | All moods, best variety | Use stems → isolate pad/strings only |
250: | **Artlist** | $10/mo | Unlimited license | Tense, Escalation | Great ambient/cinematic selection |
251: 
252: > [!CAUTION]
253: > **NEVER use copyright-claimed music.** Even "royalty-free" tracks from random sites can trigger Content ID. Stick to the sources above. Always verify the license before using any track.
254: 
255: ### Fallback Search Queries by Mood
256: 
257: | Mood | Search Query |
258: |---|---|
259: | Neutral / Context | `"ambient background" OR "soft documentary" OR "lo-fi pad"` |
260: | Tense / Dangerous | `"dark ambient" OR "suspense drone" OR "ominous atmosphere"` |
261: | Philosophical / Reflective | `"melancholic piano" OR "reflective ambient" OR "contemplative cello"` |
262: | Escalation / Countdown | `"building tension" OR "rising suspense" OR "countdown music"` |
263: | Climax / Peak Reveal | `"cinematic reveal" OR "epic swell" OR "orchestral climax"` |
264: | Resolution / CTA | `"warm acoustic" OR "gentle ending" OR "peaceful outro"` |
265: 
266: ---
267: 
268: ## 8 · Decision Matrix: AI-Generated vs Library Music
269: 
270: | Factor | Use Lyria 3 (AI) | Use Library Music |
271: |---|---|---|
272: | **Mood specificity** | Need exact mood tailored to YOUR script sections | Generic mood is fine |
273: | **Duration** | Need precise length (e.g., exactly 47 seconds for a section) | Standard lengths OK (30s, 60s, 90s) |
274: | **Uniqueness** | Want zero chance of another channel using the same track | Don't care about uniqueness |
275: | **Speed** | Have time to generate + review + regenerate | Need music NOW, tight deadline |
276: | **Quality consistency** | Willing to do 2-3 takes per mood | First-pick quality guaranteed |
277: | **Copyright certainty** | 100% original, zero Content ID risk | Pre-cleared but tiny residual risk |
278: | **Cost** | Free (Lyria 3) | Free or $10-15/mo for premium |
279: 
280: ### The Hybrid Strategy (Recommended)
281: 
282: 1. **Always try Lyria 3 first** — it's free, original, and tailored to your exact needs.
283: 2. **Generate 2-3 takes per mood** — pick the best, discard the rest.
284: 3. **Fall back to library** if after 3 takes the mood still isn't right.
285: 4. **Mix and match** — some sections AI, some library. As long as mood palette is consistent, no one notices.
286: 
287: ---
288: 
289: ## 9 · Step-by-Step Workflow
290: 
291: ### Phase 1: Tag Script Sections (During Stage 3)
292: 
293: 1. Read through the finished script.
294: 2. Label each section with one of the 6 moods.
295: 3. Note the approximate duration of each section (count words ÷ 150 WPM ≈ seconds).
296: 
297: **Output format:**
298: 
299: ```
300: MUSIC MAP — [Video Title]
301: 
302: Section 1: Hook (0:00-0:30)         → Mood: NEUTRAL      → Duration: 30s
303: Section 2: Context (0:30-2:00)      → Mood: NEUTRAL      → Duration: 90s
304: Section 3: Danger (2:00-3:30)       → Mood: TENSE        → Duration: 90s
305: Section 4: Escalation (3:30-5:00)   → Mood: ESCALATION   → Duration: 90s
306: Section 5: Reveal (5:00-5:30)       → Mood: CLIMAX       → Duration: 30s
307: Section 6: Cost (5:30-6:30)         → Mood: TENSE        → Duration: 60s
308: Section 7: Philosophy (6:30-8:00)   → Mood: PHILOSOPHICAL → Duration: 90s
309: Section 8: CTA (8:00-8:30)         → Mood: RESOLUTION   → Duration: 30s
310: ```
311: 
312: ### Phase 2: Generate Music (During Stage 4)
313: 
314: 1. Open Lyria 3 (or fallback source).
315: 2. For each section, paste the matching prompt template from § 2.
316: 3. Replace `[DURATION]` with the section's duration + 10 seconds buffer.
317: 4. Generate 2-3 takes. Pick the best.
318: 5. Save to `audio/music/generated/[video_slug]_[mood]_[take].wav`.
319: 
320: ### Phase 3: Level & Assemble (During Stage 6)
321: 
322: 1. Level each segment to -18 dB:
323:    ```bash
324:    ffmpeg -i generated/[slug]_neutral_01.wav -af "volume=-18dB" -c:a pcm_s24le leveled/[slug]_neutral_leveled.wav
325:    ```
326: 2. Apply fade-in to first segment (3s) and fade-out to last segment (5s).
327: 3. Crossfade adjacent segments (2-3s overlap).
328: 4. Insert silence gaps before reveals (1-1.5s).
329: 5. Apply climax swell (+3-5 dB temporary boost).
330: 6. Export final assembled music track:
331:    ```bash
332:    # Final output: single continuous music track
333:    → audio/music/assembled/[video_slug]_music_full.wav
334:    ```
335: 
336: ---
337: 
338: ## 10 · Quality Checklist
339: 
340: Run through this before moving to final audio mix:
341: 
342: ### Music Selection
343: 
344: - [ ] Every script section has a mood tag from the 6-mood palette
345: - [ ] Music mood matches the emotional arc at EVERY point in the video
346: - [ ] Music CHANGES when the script mood changes (never one track for full video)
347: - [ ] All tracks are copyright-safe (Lyria 3 or verified library source)
348: - [ ] No tracks contain vocals, prominent melodies, or sharp percussion
349:

353: - [ ] Climax swell present (+3-5 dB temporary boost at peak)
354: - [ ] Music drops to silence before at least 3 major reveals
355: - [ ] Fade-in at video start (3 seconds)
356: - [ ] Fade-out at video end (5 seconds)
357: - [ ] Music never overpowers or competes with the voice
358:

361: - [ ] Crossfades between all mood changes (2-3 seconds)
362: - [ ] No hard cuts between music segments
363: - [ ] Swell → drop → silence before the #1 reveal

368: - [ ] All music files: WAV, 48 kHz, 24-bit, stereo

370: - [ ] No audio clipping or distortion on any segment
371: - [ ] File naming follows convention: `[slug]_[mood]_[take].wav`

374: ### The Listen Test
375: 
376: - [ ] Play the mixed video while doing something else (scrolling, making coffee)
377: - [ ] You can **feel** the mood changes but can't **hum** the melody
